primitives.verbatim_quote: --## PART 1 — METRIC CATALOG ### EPA per play (team) EPA is the change in Expected Points from before a play to after it; Expected Points is the historical average net point value of a game state defined by down, distance, and field position.

reasoning_traces.think:
EPA per play encapsulates contextual efficiency by measuring the net change in expected points from one play to the next, integrating down, distance, and field position. This provides a scalar summary of team performance that transcends raw yardage. CPOE isolates QB accuracy by subtracting expected completions from actual, controlling for target difficulty. Together, they form a dual signal: EPA for team-wide drive sustainability and CPOE for quarterback precision. DAVE introduces a principled shrinkage mechanism that blends early-season volatility with preseason priors, stabilizing forecasts. These primitives are mathematically grounded in stochastic efficiency kernels, where EPA is a cumulative random walk, CPOE a normalized deviation, and DAVE a Bayesian posterior with fixed prior. Failure modes include model misalignment (e.g., CPOE model dependency), filtering artifacts (e.g., EPA garbage-time inclusion), and temporal drift (e.g., outdated preseason priors).
